Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Lisa Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, VP of Exploration; Tom Reilly, VP of Marketing; Rachel Kim, Chief Sustainability Officer; and David Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust realized prices for oil at $82.50 per barrel and gas at $3.25 per MCF, bolstered by our hedging programs. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on environmental performance, including zero reportable spills and strong remediation efforts. Our midstream segment saw impressive transportation volumes and infrastructure advancements. We are focused on capital expenditure guidance that prioritizes high-return projects. Further, refining operations excelled with high throughput and margins. EBITDA surged 28% year-over-year due to key drivers like production growth. We are advancing exploration and drilling with standout well results. Finally, we are taking steps to accelerate ESG initiatives, making significant headway on emissions reductions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Steve Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Lisa. As Lisa mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.2 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $900 million in free cash flow and returned $400 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $8.5 billion in debt and $2.1 billion in cash.

Let me dive deeper into some key financial highlights. Starting with realized pricing, which remains a cornerstone of our cash flow generation in this volatile macro environment. For the quarter, our consolidated realized oil price averaged $76.45 per barrel, up 8% sequentially from $70.80 in Q1 but down 12% year-over-year from $86.95 in Q2 2023. On the natural gas side, we realized $2.35 per MCF, a 5% improvement from $2.24 in Q1 but still 22% below last year's $3.02 amid persistent oversupply pressures.

These realized prices reflect a blend of strong benchmark support for oil—NYMEX WTI settled at an average of $81.25/bbl, while Dated Brent averaged $85.60—tempered by regional basis differentials, quality adjustments, and transportation constraints. Our hedging program played a pivotal role here, protecting roughly 55% of our oil production and 40% of our gas volumes at favorable floors, which added approximately $450 million in pre-tax hedging gains for the quarter. Without hedges, our realized oil price would have been $72.10/bbl—a 6% haircut—and gas at $1.95/MCF, exposing us to the full brunt of mid-quarter WTI dips below $77 on Red Sea disruptions and OPEC+ compliance uncertainties.

Breaking it down by commodity and region: In the Permian Basin, 72% of Q2 oil production, we delivered $78.20/bbl realized, benefiting from narrowing WTI Midland differentials to just -$0.75/bbl, down from -$2.10 in Q1. This compression stems from the full-ramp of ExxonMobil's Matterhorn and EPIC Crude Oil Pipeline expansions, which alleviated bottlenecks and boosted takeaway capacity to over 6.5 MMbbl/d. We saw minimal quality deductions—our WTI-equivalent Permian sweet crude fetched a $0.50 premium net of gravity adjustments, with our blend averaging 42° API. Hedging impact: 65% swapped at a $72.00/bbl floor via NYMEX WTI swaps, capturing $6.2 million in gains as spot prices softened post-Ukraine-related supply fears.

In the Eagle Ford, 18% of production, realized $73.10/bbl, pressured by wider Corpus Christi differentials at -$1.45/bbl due to refinery maintenance at Valero's Three Rivers facility and competing Eagle Ford condensate grades. Our higher-BTU Eagle Ford oil, 38°-40° API, incurred a $1.20/bbl LOC penalty, but our collars—50% of volumes protected between $68-$82/bbl—limited downside, contributing $2.8 million in value. Blended oil differential was -$4.80/bbl to WTI, improved from -$6.20 in Q1, driven by 15% higher Corpus loading volumes and fixed-fee EPL contracts. Hedging muted a 10% Q-o-Q benchmark drop.

Year-to-date, oil hedges have locked in 52% of 2024 volumes at $71.50/bbl average swap price, with an additional 20% in two-way collars, average floor $69, cap $84. This conservative approach—targeting 50-60% coverage—shields our $2.2 billion capex program while preserving upside to Brent's $90+ potential amid tightening global inventories, OPEC spare capacity now at 5.8 MMbbl/d per IEA estimates.

For natural gas: Haynesville Shale, 65% of Q2 gas production, $2.45/MCF realized, up 7% Q-o-Q on stronger LOCAP basis, +15% to Henry Hub at +$0.12/MMBtu. High-BTU content, 1,150 BTU/scf, earned a $0.18 premium, though pipeline constraints on GTN and Texas Gas Transmission shaved $0.10. Hedging: 45% fixed-price swaps at $2.60/MMBtu NYMEX Henry Hub equivalent, yielding $18 million in settlements amid a mild shoulder season.

Appalachia Marcellus/Utica, 25% of production, $1.85/MCF, dragged by TETCO M-3 basis weakness at -$0.65 to Henry Hub from oversupplied Northeast markets and Dominion's compressor upgrades lagging. Our dry gas, 1,030 BTU, faced $0.15/BTU shrinkage penalties, but 35% collar protection, $2.20-$3.50 floor/ceiling, buffered a 15% spot price plunge tied to EIA-reported storage surplus of 450 Bcf above five-year averages. Corporate differential was -$0.35/MCF to Henry Hub, $2.58 average, with LLS exposure minimal. Q2 hedging gains totaled $32 million, covering 42% of volumes at $2.55/MMBtu average.

Our hedging philosophy emphasizes cash flow certainty over speculation. We've layered in 65% protection for H2 2024 oil at $70/bbl swaps and 50% for 2025 at $68/bbl, using a mix of financial swaps 80%, collars 15%, and puts 5% transacted via CME and ICE platforms. This de-risks our FCF yield target of 12-15% at $70 WTI/$2.50 gas, funding $800 million in Permian rig adds and Eagle Ford refracs without equity dilution.

Regionally, Permian oil basis should tighten further with Gray Oak Phase II online Q4, potentially lifting differentials to -$0.40. Haynesville gas could rebound 20%+ in Q4 on winter demand and LNG export ramps, Freeport LNG at 95% utilization. However, we remain vigilant on downside risks—Middle East escalations could spike Brent 10-15%, but U.S. shale supply growth, Permian +400 Mbbl/d Q-o-Q per EIA, caps upside. In summary, realized prices underscore the efficacy of disciplined hedging amid volatility, delivering $1.8 billion in adjusted EBITDA—up 5% Q-o-Q.

Speaking of EBITDA, it came in at $1.85 billion for the quarter, representing a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $1.44 billion in Q3 last year. On a trailing twelve-month basis, adjusted EBITDA now stands at $7.2 billion, up 22% YoY. This outperformance underscores the strength of our high-margin portfolio and execution of our capital-efficient growth strategy amid a supportive commodity price environment.

Key drivers behind this $410 million YoY uplift: First, commodity price realizations added approximately $220 million. Our realized crude oil price averaged $82.50 per barrel, up 18% from $70 in Q3 '23, driven by Brent sustaining above $80/bbl—peaking near $90 in September amid tighter-than-expected global inventories and ongoing OPEC+ production cuts of over 2 million bpd. Natural gas realizations held steady at $3.25 per Mcf, benefiting from robust LNG export demand out of the Gulf Coast, though some softness in Appalachia due to regional oversupply from associated gas flaring cuts. Overall, blended realized price of $65.40 per boe rose 16% YoY, with hedges covering 60% of oil volumes at a $75/bbl floor providing a buffer against volatility.

Production growth accounted for another $120 million. We averaged 285,000 boe/d in Q3, a 12% YoY increase from 255,000 boe/d, with oil comprising 68% of the mix—up from 65% as we prioritized liquids-rich plays. In the Permian Basin, output hit 180,000 boe/d, up 18% YoY, fueled by the ramp-up of our Black River asset acquisition. We've drilled 25% longer laterals averaging 12,000 feet, achieving D&C costs of $650 per lateral foot—down 10% YoY—thanks to proprietary 'smart frac' technology integrating real-time fiber-optic diagnostics and AI-optimized proppant placement. This lowered Permian breakevens to $42/bbl WTI.

Eagle Ford contributed 55,000 boe/d, up 8% YoY, with enhanced oil recovery pilots using CO2 injection boosting recoveries by 15% in Karnes County. Offshore Gulf of Mexico saw a 5,000 boe/d uptick from Lucius field tie-backs, though hurricane-related shut-ins cost ~2,000 boe/d temporarily—mitigated by rapid-restart protocols. Appalachia volumes flat at 45,000 boe/d, curtailing some dry gas amid sub-$2.50/MMBtu Henry Hub, redirecting to higher-return oil windows.

On costs, $90 million in EBITDA through efficiencies. LOE dropped to $8.20/boe, 12% YoY reduction, driven by enterprise-wide digital twin initiative using predictive analytics to optimize artificial lift and reduce workovers by 20%. G&A at $2.10/boe, flat YoY despite inflation on tubulars and sand, benefiting from shared services post-acquisition. Cash margins expanded to $52/boe from $42/boe.

Headwinds: offshore services inflation added ~$15 million from higher GoM rig rates, $10 million one-time integration. Offset by hedging and inventory management, turning drill-ready locations 15% faster via pad drilling. This positions us to return 50% of FCF—$1.2 billion in dividends and buybacks—while reducing net debt to 0.8x EBITDA from 1.2x. Q4 guide 290-300,000 boe/d, Permian growth offsetting seasonal Appalachia.

Turning to our refining segment, which delivered strong results amid volatility. Our downstream spans six refineries, Nelson Complexity Index 11.2 average, including flagship 600,000 bpd Gulf Coast Port Arthur and Midwest PADD 2 facilities optimized for Canadian heavy sour crudes. Processed diverse slate: WTI, Maya, Western Canadian Select, benefiting from contango in WCS differential, $18/bbl discount to WTI.

Throughput: average gross 1.18 million bpd, up 4% QoQ from 1.14 million, flat YoY. Utilization 92%, upper end of 88-94% target, reliability 99.2% via AI-driven asset performance management. Gulf Coast 620,000 bpd, 6% QoQ post-turnaround, stronger distillate demand, exports to Latin America. Midwest 320,000 bpd steady on discounted Canadian imports. JV Rotterdam 240,000 bpd equivalent, up 3% on Dubai sweet. Q3 expect 1.20-1.25 million bpd, no major weather.

Margins: segment EBITDA $850 million, $18.50/bbl, 15% QoQ lift. Net refining margin $12.80/bbl 3-2-1, outperforming USGC $11.50 by 11%. Gulf Coast crack $15.20/bbl from $13.80, gasoline $22/bbl on driving demand, inventories drew 5 million bbl; diesel $18/bbl shipping recovery. Yields: distillates 54% up 2 pts, gasoline 24%, clean 82%, hydrocracker >95%. Hedged 60% gasoline/diesel cracks $14/bbl floor, $200 million protection. Rotterdam $16/bbl GRM vs Singapore $14.50, Red Sea ULSD premiums. Headwind $2/bbl natgas for hydrogen, mitigated 50% captive. YTD 12% above 2023.

Efficiency: cash opex $4.40/bbl, down 8% YoY below $4.65 guide. Digital transformation Phase 1, AspenTech APC-plus, ML crude assay, coker yields +1.5 pts. Energy intensity 85,000 BTU/bbl from 92,000, Scope 1+2 20% cut by 2028 via cogeneration Port Arthur 25 MW. Turnarounds front-loaded, 45-day Illinois alkylation, UOP catalysts +3 RON. Maintenance capex $120 million Q2, $450 million FY. Transition: 10,000 bpd renewable diesel co-processing, LCFS $50 million annualized. 15-20% biofuels by 2027. FCF $650 million Q2, funding 60% dividend/buyback. H2 cracks $13-16/bbl, demand +1.2 MMbpd YoY IEA, OPEC+ feedstock.

On capital expenditure guidance, for 2025 $4.8-5.2 billion, 5-8% below 2024 $5.3 billion midpoint, capital discipline amid moderating costs. Upstream 95%: D&C $3.7-4.0 billion 75-77%, Permian $2.8-3.0 billion, 450-500 wells, 3,200+ locations Delaware/Midland. D&C $750-800/lateral ft, 15% YoY improve, 12,000 ft laterals, 3,500-4,000 lb/ft proppant, PermianMax +10-15% IP. Eagle Ford $400-450 million 80-90 wells Pearsall 1.2-1.5 MMBoe EUR. GoM $500 million tie-backs Winterfell/Lobster <$45 breakeven.

Exploration $400-500 million: GoM $200 million two wildcats Chevron Anchor, 100-200 MMboe 25-35% IRR $70 oil. Namibia Block 1 $150 million Venus-2 500 MMboe. Maintenance $400-450 million electrification Permian 20% Scope 1 cut, Energy Transfer NGL JV. Midstream/downstream $250-300 million Bakken rail, Permian CCS IRA credits.

Permian 60% capex, 12 rigs 20 frac, 220-240k Boe/d '25 end, $35-40 half-cycle. Eagle/Bakken 15% 10-12% IRR. Offshore/intl 25% 20-40% IRR. Portfolio IRR 25-30%, half-cycle <9 months Permian. >20% IRR $60 WTI NPV10. $65 oil FCF 15-18%; $50 flex 20% rig stack. Digital twins SLB Delfi 2-3 days off spud-rig. 10% transition $500 million electrification DAC Lobster. 2026-2028 $15-16 billion cum, 5% CAGR 650k Boe/d, 50-60% FCF return.

Before wrapping, a note on environmental performance. ESG stewardship core, pathway net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2040. Q3 zero reportable spills portfolio-wide, continuation Q2 streak, lowest in 15-year history. Nine months three minor 42 bbls, down 78% from 192 bbls 2022. Spill vol 0.08 bbls/mmboe < API 0.1, outperforms Exxon 0.15 Chevron 0.22.

TRIR 0.18/200k man-hours Q3, 10% better Q3'22, 35% below IOGP 0.28. LTIR 0.05 zero downtime. 25% increase drone pipeline inspections 8,000 miles Permian.

Permian one 15-bbl crude spill July corroded flowline pigging, contained 30 min, 100% recovery, no impact EPA sampling, <$250k from $50 million accrual. GoM Thunder Horse/Shenzi zero, ROV acoustic leak detection -40% risk. Eagle Ford 27-bbl produced water tank overfill, bioremediation Oil Spill Eater 98% 45 days.

North Sea zero, OSPAR compliant, Magnus decommissioning zero findings. YTD remediation $4.2 million up slight from $3.8 million, $15-20 million annual, 99% recovery 'no further action'. AI Schlumberger Delfi corrosion forecast -22% failures, phased-array UT 95% offshore risers. Zero Spill double-sheaved frac hoses Halliburton CleanStim, $12 million dispersants.

De-risks ops WTI $75, zero fines vs industry $1.2 million API. SEC disclosures spill Scope 3 methane <0.5%. $25 million 2024 capex DAS 60% US gathering <2 hour detection. Competitive moat 15% ROCE upstream.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Rodriguez for an operational update.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Steve. On the operational front, we continue to execute effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Blackhawk Federal 7H-12 online, expected to contribute significantly to production growth. Progress on cost reductions, with LOE efficiencies via digital tools.

Now I'll turn it over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for exploration.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mike. Excited about our program. Walking through exploration and drilling: Q2 28 new wells online, IP30 1,850 Boe/d per well up 12% Q1 1,650. Laterals 12,500 ft 15% YoY increase. Spud-rig-release 18 days Delaware vs 22 year ago. Capex $320 million Q2, Permian D&C $850/lateral ft lowest peer, beat EOG 8%.

Standout Blackhawk Federal 7H-12 Waddell Ridge Wolfcamp AXYL IP30 3,200 Boe/d 82% oil, 24-hr peak 4,100. EUR 1.8 MMboe decline analysis Pioneer analogs. 110 lb/ft 55 stages ApexFlow resin-coated Liberty, propped height +25%, declines 65% first 90 days vs basin 75%.

Midland Pinon Draw five-well IP30 1,450 Boe/d 75% oil EUR >1.2 MMboe Spraberry/Woodford 4D seismic OXY 15 locations. Cycle 16 days spud-TD Walker Ridge Rig #47 automated.

Eagle Ford Karnes Eaglehawk 3H-8 IP30 2,100 Boe/d 45% oil/45% NGLs +18% type curve, super-laterals 15,000+ ft 95 lb/ft, oil-rich 2.5x capex return strip.

GoM Lobster-2 appraisal 5,200 Boe/d IP7 Miocene, Chevron partner 50 MMboe Q4'25 tie-back Noble drillship MPD $45 million 10% under.

98% success 32 gross Q2, YTD 97% Continental tier. ML Palantir Foundry landing/frac -20% parent-child. Dissolvable diverters SLB cluster eff 92% from 85% fiber. Proppant 105 lb/ft to 120 H2. Electric frac ProFrac -15k diesel gal/pad Scope 1 -25%, water recycle 85% XRI brackish.

Future: 120-130 wells 2024 70% Permian, 3 Delaware/Midland 1 non-op 1 Eagle end-year. D&C $1.4-1.5 billion FCF $75 WTI. Inventory 4,200+ <$50 breakeven 1,800 Tier 1 Permian. $450 million bolt-on 12k acres Northern Delaware 400 loc $15k/acre < Occidental CrownRock. Permian IRR >60% 6-8 mo payback. Hedge 55% 2025 oil $74 40% gas $3.00. Flex rigs $70+ up $65- down. Positions 18-22% growth 95k Boe/d year-end FCF.

We recently completed successful seismic in Permian Basin Delaware, planning 120-130 exploration wells next year, potential significant reserves.

Finally, to Tom Reilly on marketing.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Elena. Focused on optimizing to maximize production value. Strong demand for renewable diesel in Gulf Coast, expanding customer base, strengthening relationships. Impact significant, with LCFS credits and biofuels pivot.

Now to Rachel Kim on sustainability.

Rachel Kim: Thank you, Tom. Committed to reducing footprint, sustainable ops. Significant progress GHG emissions, renewable investments, water management, biodiversity. Detailed ESG update: net-zero Scope 1/2 2050, 35% by 2030 50% 2040 from 2020 45 million t CO2e.

Q3 Scope 1/2 10.2 million t, YTD -12% vs Q3'23 cum -18% 2020, ahead 2025 15-20%. Methane intensity 0.18 kg/BOE from 0.32 2020 < IOGP 0.25. Flaring 0.5% gross gas -65% YoY > OGCI end routine 2025.

US 55% upstream Permian 1,200 wells drone OGI GHGSat 1,200 leaks mitigated -28% YoY Scope 1 -22%. Electrification 40% rigs hybrid 150 MW solar-storage Delaware Occidental Stratos lithium baseload -150k t CO2e/yr drilling -8-10%.

North Sea Buzzard/Jotun -25% YoY NPD, subsea tiebacks WAG Rosebank shore electrification Sullom Voe zero Scope 1 '26. Middle East ADNOC -40% flaring auto-ignition VRUs UAE net-zero. LNG Qatar/Australia Scope 2 GE LM9000 H2 blend 20% today 30% '27 -15%/train.

$450 million 2024 ESG capex +20% YoY VFDs 85% pumps/compressors 5-7% savings. CCUS Polaris Hub Chevron Denbury 2.1 million t YTD amine Class VI 5 Mtpa '26 DAC Eagle Climeworks. Delfi digital twins flaring -35% AI shut-in.

Value accretive EU CBAM IRA 45Q $120 million 5-yr, de-risk activist. OGMP 2.0 Level 5 70% S&P ESG #23 +15. Carbon intensity $9/t from $12 $250 million avoided. 20-22% YE $600 million 2025 double CCUS 60% offshore electric. Feb report SBTi Scope 3.

Also tying to environmental: zero spills, TRIR 0.18, etc., as Steve noted, with drone inspections, AI corrosion, Zero Spill.

Over to David Patel on technology.

David Patel: Thank you, Rachel. Leveraging tech for efficiency, cost reduction, safety. Investing automation, data analytics, AI ops optimization. Exploring carbon capture storage, digital twins SLB Delfi, ML Palantir frac, electric frac, SCADA digital twins 70% 15k miles pipeline anomaly AI drone ILI 20% crude +5-7 yr life ESG SEC. Fiber DAS leak detection methane -40%.

Operator, ready for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on realized prices and hedging impact?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, John. Steve covered the headlines, but to add, our 55% oil 40% gas hedge coverage added $450 million gains, Permian $78.20/bbl narrow diffs EPIC Matterhorn, Eagle $73.10 collars key. YTD 52% locked $71.50, H2 65% $70, de-risks FCF 12-15%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Amy Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Amy Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA drivers going forward?

Steve Harlan: Amy, Q3 $1.85 billion +28% YoY from prices $220 million, production $120 million Permian 180k, costs $90 million LOE $8.20. Q4 290-300k, sub-$45 breakevens FCF strong returns 50%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Brian Lee: Could you please provide more color on refining performance?

Mike Rodriguez: Brian, throughput 1.18 million bpd 92% util, margins $12.80/bbl > benchmark, distillates 54%, renewable diesel start LCFS. Efficiency $4.40/bbl, digital yields up, H2 constructive $13-16 cracks.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Ramirez with Energy Insights. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: How will the results of the exploration program affect future strategy?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: John, Blackhawk 3,200 IP30 EUR 1.8 MMboe, Pinon 1,450, Lobster appraisal de-risks 50 MMboe. 4,200+ inventory, bolt-on adds 400 loc, guides 18-22% growth, flex rigs economics >60% IRR Permian core.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Torres with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Laura Torres: What is the outlook for midstream transportation and infrastructure?

Steve Harlan: Thanks, Laura. Midstream $450 million EBITDA +22% YoY 28% total, volumes 2.8 MBOE/d +18% YoY. Crude 1.5 million bpd +25% Permian Whitten 850k 92%, gas 4.2 Bcf/d +12% Mountain Valley 1.8, NGL 750k. Permian 55%, Appalachia 25%. Capex $1.2 billion YTD $4.5 billion FY, Apex Link 300-mile 400k bpd Nederland 12 million storage Jones Act, Delaware Phase III 550 MMcf/d GE H-class, Appalachia NGL $250 million Mariner. Digital SCADA 70% 15k miles -15% costs drone ILI. ROIC >12% 85% fixed 12-yr contracts, $2 billion MLP dropdown 8-10x. 10-15% vol CAGR '27 Permian D&C LNG. Raised EBITDA $6.5-6.8 billion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Patel: Could you elaborate on sustainability targets?

Rachel Kim: Mark, Scope 1/2 -18% cum, methane 0.18 kg/BOE, flaring 0.5%. Permian drone GHGSat -28%, electrification 40% rigs 150 MW solar. North Sea -25%, CCUS 2.1 million t, $450 million capex VFDs DAC. On track 20-22% YE, value $120 million credits OGMP Level 5.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Kline with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kline: What are the key technology initiatives?

David Patel: Sarah, AI ML Palantir frac optimization -20% interference, dissolvable SLB 92% clusters, Delfi twins flaring -35%, electric fleets water 85%, SCADA digital 70% pipelines, DAS methane. Efficiency safety ESG aligned.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Wong with BMO Capital. Please go ahead.

David Wong: More on capex guidance and returns?

Steve Harlan: David, 2025 $4.8-5.2 billion, upstream 95% Permian $2.8-3.0 billion 450-500 wells $750-800/ft PermianMax +10-15% IP. Portfolio 25-30% IRR <9 mo payback, >20% $60 WTI. Flat 2026-28 $15-16 billion 5% CAGR 650k production returns 50-60% FCF.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Lisa Chen for closing remarks.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
